title: Make a decision with a Python function
objective: Follow a function call, see how a condition selects a return value, and store the result in a dictionary.

steps.title: Choose one message
steps.instruction: A function gives a name to a block of code. The name points in the parentheses is a parameter. When the function is called with 8, Python gives points the value 8. Predict which return statement runs. The return statement gives a value back to the caller and ends that call.
steps.check: Explain what happens when points is exactly 10. Then change 8 to 12 in your draft and predict the new result.

exercise.prompt: What text does the original programme print?
exercise.hint: Compare 8 with 10. The indented return runs only when the condition is true.

frames.caption: Call result with the argument 8. The assignment waits for a return value.
Inside the call, points is 8, so points >= 10 is false.
Return try again. The function call now ends.
Python has assigned the return value to message. Print it.

steps.title: Look up a result by name
steps.instruction: A dictionary stores values under keys. Here, the keys are learner names and the values are scores. Square brackets ask the dictionary for the value under a particular key. Find the key Sam, then predict the value shown in the output.
steps.check: Add a new name with a score. Change the lookup to that name. Compare your prediction with the result.

exercise.prompt: What number does the original lookup print?
exercise.hint: Read the value to the right of the colon after the key "Sam".

frames.caption: Create the dictionary and assign it to scores.
Look up the key Sam and assign its value to result.
Print the value associated with result.
